page.layout: One column of running text, with verse set in italic between the paragraphs. A running head at the top, the page number at the top left, and the catchword "Epodus" at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: angelum vocat.Alij filiam iustitiæ fecerunt,nomen habet ἐκ τῆς δικαιοσύνης[?],quia cuique distribuit sua præmia,& scelerum pœnas.Itaque alij ad fatum retulere,vt esse quandam occultā,quæ discurrat in rebus humanis diuino consilio, rerum euentus limitans, & actionum humanarum progressum moderans. Hesiodus filiam facit Oceani & Noctis.vide Pausaniam in Atticis de eius simulachro,quo facit Epigramma illud.

p.i: Me lapidem quondam Perseæ aduexêre trophæum, Vt fierem bello: nunc ego sum Nemesis.
At sicut Græcis victoribus asto trophæum, Puniofic Perseas vaniloquos Nemesis.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~10 letters] Redit ad Perseï historiam quam absoluit: docet quomodo ad Hyperboreos venerit Minerua duce, quid illic egerit, quomodo etiam sit reuersus in Seriphũ. Danaës filius Perseus est, de quo vide Arati Phænomena.Boccat.lib.12.cap.25.totam fabulam persequitur: nullus tamen meminit huius profectionis ad Hyperboreos: Referunt autem omnes Danaën ex Ioue concepisse,& quum enixa esset Perseum,inclusam fuisse ab Acrisio in arcam & mari expositam, delatamque in Seriphum insulam, vbi a rege Polydecte seruata fuit, vna cum filio: ibi educatus Perseus, quum aliquando apud regem cænaret, aliisque alia ad cœnam afferrent,promisit ipse Medusæ caput: ad quod a rege compulsus, vt promissum præstaret, abiit ergo ad Hyperboreos & caput Gorgonis attulit, cuius tetro conspectu omnes Seriphij in lapides commutati sunt. Ouid. 4. Metamorph. vide scholia Græca.

[illegible, ~10 letters] Medusa vna ex sororibus mortalis fuit: itaque a Perseo decollata. Tres autem traduntur fuisse filiæ Phorcynis, Euryale Stheno, & Medusa sorores, quorum capita draconum squamis obsita fuere: dentes, suum instar, alatæ, intuentes in saxa vertebant. Seruius eas circa Atlantem montem in Africa collocat: ac vnum omnes tres tantum habuisse oculum. Serenus pariformes omnes facit.de his vide Zezen in Hesiod.
Λίθων θάνατον.) Nam Seriphios in lapides commutauit, ipsum etiam Polydecten regem.

page.notes: The Greek gloss labels before the paragraphs starting "Redit" and "Medusa" are not legible letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The Greek in the first paragraph is uncertain and marked [?]. "Puniofic" is printed as one word and is kept as printed. The last line "Epodus" is a catchword and is also shown in the bottom margin, so it appears in main_text only as a line of the page's furniture and can be removed if it should not repeat.
